severity_rationale: C4 Low: griefing/DoS path requiring active adversary to spend gas repeatedly on a contingent operation (setStakedId is a rare governance action). C4 guidance: 'Migration blocking / griefing → Medium if realistic, Low if costly for attacker.' Here the attacker must front-run each governance attempt at roughly 2x gas per cycle indefinitely, and the owner has a trivial off-chain mitigation (pause() before setStakedId). No direct fund loss; principal and accrued rewards remain owed to stakers. The unresponsive-staker variant is not attacker-driven — it is simply a missing forced-exit admin path. Classified Low because the operational deadlock is real but costly to sustain and mitigable by a single pause() call.
title: setStakedId can be blocked indefinitely by a single 1-unit staker, front-running or simply refusing to exit
description: setStakedId(newId) reverts if totalStaked > 0. emergencyWithdraw is the only staker exit, and it must be initiated by the staker (or their approved operator). There is no owner-triggered forceExit and pause() is not an enforced precondition of setStakedId. Two variants of the same blocker emerge: (1) Unresponsive staker — one or more holders with lost keys, dead smart-contract wallets, or simple inaction leave totalStaked > 0 and block setStakedId indefinitely. (2) Active griefer — an adversary observing the owner's setStakedId mempool broadcast front-runs with stake(1), causing the call to revert; attacker then unstakes, pays ~2x gas, and repeats on every attempt. Because pause is not required, an unobservant operator can be caught. The module's CLAUDE.md documents the 'ID change never strands principal' property intentionally; the cost is this operational deadlock.
attack_path:
Griefing path (primary): 1) Owner announces NFT-ID migration (e.g. a Balancer pool reissues the NFT). 2) Owner broadcasts setStakedId(newId) after coordinating stakers to exit, totalStaked reaches 0. 3) Attacker's mempool bot observes; submits stake(1) with higher gas priority. 4) setStakedId reverts with 'stake outstanding'. 5) Attacker unstakes at negligible reward accrual, pays ~2x gas. 6) Repeat on every subsequent attempt. Owner's only recourses: pause first (not enforced by the contract), or deploy a second NFTStaker (fragments TVL), or social (compensate griefer).

Unresponsive path: A single holder with a 1-unit stake and lost keys blocks migration with no active griefing required.
impact: Operational deadlock on NFT-ID migrations. No direct fund loss — principal and accrued rewards remain owed — but the designed migration flow cannot complete on-chain without coordinated social action.
recommendation: Require paused() == true inside setStakedId (makes stake() unavailable to front-runners while migration is pending). Additionally, consider a two-step migration: owner initiates a migration window, stakers must exit within the window, then setStakedId executes. At minimum, document prominently that operators must pause before attempting an ID change.

sanitization.rationale: Root cause is setStakedId's precondition in NFTStaker.sol. Not a 'reckless admin mistake' — this is a protocol design gap (missing paused() gate / missing forced exit) that prevents the documented migration flow from completing even if the admin acts correctly.
